title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a smooth curve over a base, and ω = Ω¹_X is its canonical bundle. The page relates two torsors.

(i) Connections on ω. These are first-order differential operators D: ω → ω⊗Ω¹ = ω² satisfying the Leibniz rule D(fω) = fDω + ω df. The difference of two of them is an O-linear map ω → ω², i.e. a section of ω. So connections on ω (equivalently, affine connections on the curve) form a torsor under ω. Grothendieck writes its sheaf of sections as P-σ(X) (or 𝒟-σ(X)).

(ii) Projective connections. These form a torsor under ω² (quadratic differentials).

The construction. To each connection D on ω, Grothendieck attaches a projective connection c_D. It is characterised as the unique projective connection for which the given section is 'horizontal'. A section of the connection torsor amounts to a lifting of the projective structure to a connection on ω, a theta-characteristic-free form of the oper or Miura picture.

Having fixed one connection D₀, he states (boxed) the transformation law
  c_{D₀+ω₁} = c_{D₀} + 2D₀(ω₁) + ω₁².
So the torsor map is quadratic, lying over the quadratic differential operator ω → ω², ω₁ ↦ 2Dω₁ + ω₁².

He checks consistency under two successive translations:
  c_{D₀+ω₁+ϖ₁} = c_{D₀+ω₁} + 2(D₀+ω₁)(ϖ₁) + ϖ₁²
             = c_{D₀} + 2D₀(ω₁+ϖ₁) + (ω₁+ϖ₁)².
This is correct.

Horizontality equation. The connection D₀+ω₁ is horizontal for the projective connection c_{D₀}+ϖ₂ iff
  2D₀(ω₁) + ω₁² = ϖ₂ (boxed).
This is a Riccati equation.

In a coordinate t: the standard connection is D_t(λ dt) = (dλ/dt) dt², i.e. D_t(ω) = dt·d(ω/dt). He begins checking the Leibniz rule (finished on the next page). There, with D = D_t + λdt and ϖ₂ = μdt², the equation becomes 2λ' + λ² = μ.

Also on the next page he compares c_{D_s} and c_{D_t} under a change of coordinate s(t):
- D_s = D_t − (s''/s')dt;
- c_{D_s} = c_{D_t} + [−2(s''/s')' + (s''/s')²]dt² = c_{D_t} − 2·Schw(s)dt².
So the Schwarzian derivative appears as the cocycle.

The upside-down columns are an unrelated, largely illegible scratch computation with α', α'', ω₁', ϖ₁'. They are probably coordinate formulas for the same transformation.

Purpose within the dossier: preparing a study of projective connections (Picard–Fuchs / hypergeometric-type second-order equations, Schwarzian). Neighbouring pages indicate the study is also in characteristic p, in connection with the Cartier operation and p-graded connections.
errors: No mathematical error. The machine transcription's middle line 'c_{D0}+D0ω1+ω1²' should read 'c_{D0}+2D0(ω1)+ω1²'; the final result is consistent.

Normalisation differs from Gunning's classical convention (projective = λ' − λ²/2 for an affine connection on the tangent bundle). Grothendieck's 2λ' + λ² corresponds to λ ↦ −λ (ω versus T) and a factor −2. This is a convention, not an error.
The intrinsic characterisation of c_D ('the unique projective connection for which the section is horizontal') is stated but not proved on this page.

ideas.what: Connections on the canonical bundle ω of a curve form a torsor under ω
ideas.modern_name: torsor of affine connections (connections on K_X)

ideas.what: Map from affine connections to projective connections, quadratic over ω → ω²: c_{D+ω₁} = c_D + 2Dω₁ + ω₁²
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1966); Miura (1968) in KdV context; Drinfeld–Sokolov, Frenkel (Miura opers)

ideas.what: Horizontality of a connection on ω for a projective connection is the Riccati equation 2λ' + λ² = μ
ideas.modern_name: Riccati equation / factorization of Sturm–Liouville operator ∂² − q = (∂+v)(∂−v)

ideas.what: Coordinate change of the induced projective connection gives the Schwarzian derivative (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative as cocycle of projective connections

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but entirely classical computation (Gunning/Riccati/Miura relation between affine and projective connections). Its only interest is as context for Grothendieck's work on projective connections near the Cartier operation, which anticipates characteristic-p oper themes. Nothing on this page itself is new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 of the verification: 'c_{D0} + D0ω1 + ω1²' should be 'c_{D0} + 2D0(ω1) + ω1²' (the underbrace groups c_{D0+ω1}).
's.t. [?] satisfaisant' — the handwriting reads 's. transformant' / 'satisfaisant'; it is the Leibniz condition D(fω) = fDω + ω df.
'P-σ(X)' may read 'P-ol(X)'; it is uncertain and denotes the sheaf or torsor of connections on ω.
Interlinear insertion: 'section du torseur des connexions D₁ : ω → ω²', i.e. connections take values in ω².
The bottom fragment 'D_0(fλ dt) = [d(ω/dt)] dt' should be read as D_t(ω) = [d(ω/dt)]·dt, with the struck-out start of the Leibniz check D_t(fω) = fD_t(ω) + … continued on the next page.
